title: One pass of Gemini over a whole match
result: It mostly missed the match - no sub-segments at all

title: Multi-pass with context caching
result: Tokens down 85%, but 241 segments - 7.5× too many

title: Built a ground-truth tool and labelled the match by hand
result: 32 segments, 64 sub-segments, 124 labels; rated the model's segments (25 of 32 got one star). Became the seed of MoveBench

title: Computer-vision anchors under a cached VLM
result: Pose and scene cuts as anchors: 58 segments, 100% coverage, 2 cents, under two minutes

title: Two-pass fix for the attention cliff
result: Failed - coverage fell to 46%

title: "Skeleton and flesh": pose plus motion, one pass
result: 25 segments for 1.3 cents. The shape the harness grew from

title: MoveHarness and MoveBench v0
result: Position F1 0.017 → 0.189 from CV grounding (a CV-only baseline: 0.213); 58.9% across 496 clips; 4,620 real-upload segments reviewed by hand. Accepted at CAISc 2026

title: Does prompt framing make a model more factual?
result: +0.43 at first, then shown to be a formatting confound (−0.02)

title: Pose-to-position classifier on ViCoS
result: 0.948 F1 on a random split, 0.044 holding out sessions. It had learned the room. Retracted

title: Adversarial de-biasing against the room
result: Session probe 0.95 → 0.70, at a cost to the task (0.44 → 0.34)

title: Audited Harmony4D's ground truth
result: The reference meshes interpenetrate in 51.7% of frames

title: What runs on a 6 GB laptop GPU
result: RTMPose 33.8 fps against BBoxMaskPose 0.71 fps

title: Masks touching as a contact detector
result: AUC 0.890, worse than plain box overlap (0.922). Dropped

title: Relative depth from PromptHMR
result: Correlates 0.95 with truth - but side-to-side error is 4–20× the depth error

title: How much does the camera matter?
result: 60.5 cm of 3D error with the wrong focal length, 8.4 cm with the right one

title: Estimating the camera per shot
result: GeoCalib: 6.1% focal error, keeps 71.5% of the gain

title: Checking 3D placement without ground truth
result: A self-check that flags bad placements at AUC 0.933

title: Where do the two people get merged?
result: 92.3% of "missed" detections were my own matching bug; the real merge is in pose de-duplication

title: Reading PromptHMR's weights
result: Its cross-person attention is trained - but to track which person is first, not how they interact

title: A full one-camera placement loop
result: 20.0 → 9.2 cm, within 25 cm on 75% of frames. Mask prompts made it worse

title: Can motion tell two grapplers apart?
result: No - AUC 0.42. In no-gi, where one body ends and the other begins isn't where the colours change

title: Off-the-shelf tools on one armbar
result: Identity holds; SAM 3 / 3.1 never recovers the trapped arm; body models collapse at 3.5 s

title: All 27 vision and 64 language layers of Qwen3.8-27B
result: About $5 of cloud GPU. The model recognised the armbar in 0 of 8 prompts

title: Ownership probes and decoders
result: Naming the athlete never helped; swapping them flips the whole person. 0 of 27 trapped arms right

title: Provenance audit of my own results
result: Found actor-ID reversals, and that the "armbar" answer was describing a triangle

title: Human State v0 on a small VLM
result: Posture: released model 36.1%, trained heads 50.0%, a probe on its frozen features 66.7%

title: Controls on the small VLM
result: Answers moved with option order and athlete swaps, and survived blank images

title: Three encoders, same crops, same tiny head
result: DINO 82.0%, Qwen 75.6%, Laya 70.9%

title: Learned temporal adapter vs interpolation
result: Interpolation won (0.825 against 0.615)

title: Weight audit of the small VLM
result: 86,433,024 vision weights identical to the public SmolVLM it's built on

title: Calibrating an AI labeller
result: Three effort levels against claims it could support; picked the middle one

title: Trial100
result: 100 sources, 4,000 seconds, 3,213 labelled claims

title: Auto-labeller: AI reviewer plus SAM 3.1
result: 8,512 frames, 49,794 people; masks good on 85.1% of audited actor-frames

title: How fast do you need to sample a fight?
result: At 2 fps about 43% of fast wrist peaks are missed; 12.5 fps holds IoU 0.981

title: Gold review by hand
result: 103 verdicts on the auto-labels; no true identity switches

title: Tangle tracker
result: Ownership in tangles 0.845 → 0.882; won blind reviews 13–2 (p ≈ 0.007)

title: Dot-assisted correction
result: 932 dots on 94 frames, propagated through video: held-out 75% → 90%, blind reviews 28–6

title: Final layer campaign: 636 jobs
result: Best layer 14, validation IoU 0.580

title: Layout audit
result: Found a token reshape that misplaced most spatial locations, and voided the results built on it

title: Depth-ordered ownership from 3D bodies
result: 280 right, 69 swapped

title: Engagement as measurable 3D relations
result: Contact by region, distance and limb threading, scored against multi-view ground truth

title: One-camera baseline
result: In-contact F1 0.85–0.92, body lock 0.80; the shuffled-partner control drops to ≤ 0.05

title: Fixing one error at a time with ground truth
result: Depth between the two people is what breaks it: 14.5 cm, against 5.0 cm side to side

title: Monocular depth, alone and combined
result: Alone, it failed its pre-registered test. Combined with SAM 3D Body it passed all six: distance 10.0 → 3.9 cm

title: A learned placement correction
result: A small network that moves and turns each body: distance 3.95 → 3.17 cm on 1,068 held-out views. Public on Hugging Face

title: New people
result: Trained on one pair, it keeps about two-thirds of its gain on a different pair doing MMA (5.07 → 4.30 cm)

title: Ground work, with no 3D truth
result: Combined depth lifts mount 0.14 → 0.29, closed guard 0.20 → 0.33, back control 0.39 → 0.64, without false positives

title: Beyond grappling
result: Ballroom dancing: distance 2.7 cm, touching F1 0.96. Sword fighting 2.4 m apart: distance right to about 4%. Hugging still fails - the arms hide

title: Does time fill in hidden limbs?
result: Not on its own; a per-frame head helps a little in tangles (5.39 → 4.81 cm, exploratory)

title: A trust flag without ground truth
result: Flags bad frames at AUROC 0.795 held out, 0.76 on new people

title: Engagement at range
result: Distance right to about 4% with the two people 2.4 m apart - but it misses its absolute pre-registered bars

title: Six layers, one camera
result: Tracking, masks, 2D and 3D bodies, contact events, and VLM narration that cites the measured events

title: 29 clips across kinds of engagement
result: Hugs, ballroom, West Coast Swing, karate, MMA and grappling; every clip passed per-layer quality gates; one VHS clip retired as a documented failure

title: Scored against truth on 12
result: 0 identity switches, masks IoU 0.69–0.90, 3D limbs 2.9–5.2 cm; karate's 6 strikes all found within 0.2 s

title: Where it's hard
result: Hugs hide arms, strikes are hard to time, and one dancer in front of the other throws depth off by 16–33 cm

title: Token-layout audit before any probe
result: Every image patch mapped back to its row and column on all five models' processors

title: Ask five VLMs, then probe them layer by layer
result: The object's word holds depth (0.172 abs-rel; MoGe-2 0.138). Asked, Qwen3.8-27B is no better than a guess from the name (0.370 vs 0.394). $4.07

title: Spatial fine-tunes against their base models
result: SpatialAxiom-9B's spoken depth beats its base (0.233 vs 0.344) with the same probes inside; the SpatialVLM-recipe reproduction doesn't help here

title: Decoders tested on a kind of scene they never saw
result: They don't carry over: 2 of 50 pass. Depth error on new scenes 0.73–5.3, against 0.20–0.57 for the model's own answer

title: A dense head on Qwen3.8's own vision tower
result: Depth per pixel 0.186 vs MoGe-2's 0.096; joints 69% vs ViTPose+'s 96%. The geometry is there, but coarse

title: Every question in a second wording
result: The findings hold. SpatialAxiom is the steadiest; the SpatialVLM-recipe model loses 10 points on relations asked the other way round

title: Decoders trained on four kinds of scene
result: Still no transfer (1 of 26), but variety helps: indoor depth error 5.32 → 0.45 once synthetic rooms are in training
